explicit_validation.explanation: Both LLM evaluation (feature extraction verification) and human evaluation (sanity check) are conducted, but they serve different purposes and are never compared or validated against each other. The human evaluation is a manual sanity check on dataset quality, while LLM evaluation is used for automatic dataset verification.

prompts.notes: Detailed FEATURE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT templates are provided in Appendix figures for each reasoning category (Arithmetic, World-Knowledge, Temporal) and discourse style (Uni-Speaker, Multi-Speaker)

guidelines.notes: Assessment criteria described as: (i) fluency, (ii) implicit support for the queried fact, and (iii) absence of explicit leakage. But no detailed scoring rubric or annotation guidelines are provided.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluation focused on verifying that generated documents contain recoverable implicit facts during dataset construction. Human evaluation focused on manual sanity checking of dataset quality for fluency and implicit relationship preservation. The two evaluation methods serve completely different purposes and assess different aspects.
